tolerance: Every graded output is categorical or an integer count, so comparisons are exact: readiness and system readiness words, gate status words, next gate, chain link status / own_ok / exception, the presence or absence of a rule for a system (and its severity and gate where checked), reason-code sets per link and their due flags, punch predicates (effcat, closed_valid, transferred, void), index and frontier membership and order, dossier ids and the save outcome. The only arithmetic is whole-day differences of calendar dates (spec 4.10, ages and closure durations) and counts of rows or findings: integers, compared exactly. mean_closure_d is the arithmetic mean of those integers rounded to one decimal (spec 4.10); the three reference means in this corpus (7.0, 4.0 and 9.5) are exactly representable in binary floating point, so that comparison is exact as well. No tolerance was chosen to make a case pass. Check names address the outputs of spec 13.2: 'rule:<id>:<system>' is presence for that system, with an optional fourth part only where the finding points at an id the input itself carries (a requirement id, a punch id, a review-decision id or an evidence item id); no check depends on how the tool spells an internal field path. 'link_reasons' is the set of reason codes of that link, sorted here for a stable file and to be compared as a set.
not_benchmarked: COM-R-068 MODEL_INTEGRITY: a self-check over the rule corpus ('an edge or policy names a missing item'). No input state can trigger it, so the corpus only asserts its absence.

Package transport (spec 7.1): the explicit Load, the section mapping, the replaced/unmapped/ignored report, the digest and the conflict rule. Cases hand the `imported` projection directly, as section 13.1 allows; package cases belong to TZ-project-package 7 QA.

Written register shapes (spec 7.3) and the saved `turnover_dossiers[].chain` block: the corpus grades the save outcome (ok / refused, and whether a name is listed as offending) but not the written field values.

The 'Convert punch conditions to the punch register' action (spec 10, panel 6), 'Assemble index' as an interactive action and the permalink: actions and UI state, not expressible in the 13.1 input vocabulary. Assembly itself is graded through the assembled index of each case.
Rendering, layout, mobile behaviour, figures, report pagination, the seven languages and the Python export decline (spec 14).
Messages, next actions and basis strings of findings: only rule id, legacy id, system, severity, gate and chain link are graded (spec 13.2).

Whether the punch categories, the eight links, the dossier sections and the severities are the right engineering choice: author method (spec 14). Nothing here demonstrates conformity with any cited standard.
Contents of referenced documents, test sheets or certificates - the tool never reads them (spec 2.3).

Sibling vocabularies beyond the field names of spec 3.5 (deviation status words, functional-test result words, vendor-document status/maturity words): the corpus uses the values the spec lists; a mismatch with a sibling tool is an integration issue for the coordinator (spec 14 and the spec's open questions 1-3).

With two dossiers for one system (COM-R-161) the rules read the first row in state order (spec changelog 2026-09-23); COM-R-101 and the save outcome are graded, COM-R-162..177 are not, because the second row of that case is empty and grading them would only restate the first row.

Whether a flag whose target_kind is outside the runtime FLAG_KINDS list of diagram-project.js is additionally reported as COM-R-182: the spec requires the reopening (4.8, acceptance 5). punch_item is in fact listed by the runtime, so the case flags-reopen-l2-l4-l6-l7 simply does not assert that absence.
Which fields a test-derived evidence record carries beyond status and reference (spec 4.4 names only those two), so no case makes COM-R-057 or COM-R-058 depend on a derived criterion or owner.

The `system` field of a project-level finding (COM-R-048, COM-R-170): the spec changelog of 2026-09-23 settles it on the v1 behaviour frozen by acceptance criterion 1, and 13.2 does not grade that field.
coverage: 121 cases (119 by the reference author, 2 added by adjudication 2026-09-23). Rules with a triggering case: 120 of 121; the one exception is COM-R-068 MODEL_INTEGRITY, which no input can trigger. Rules with a near-miss case that asserts absence: 121 of 121 (all). The case count is above the 40-90 band the brief suggests because the tool carries 120 rule ids (67 retained v1 rules and 53 v2 rules) and each needs a trigger and a near-miss. Headline claims: presets P-A..P-D reproduce every 'Expected' line of spec 9 (readiness, first broken link and its reason codes, counted and uncounted findings, ages 7/12/10/4/21 d, dossier id TOD-chw-pump-p-201, index sizes 18/1/1/1/1); acceptance 6 (chain_enforce yes vs no on one state: severity and verdict change, link statuses do not); acceptance 5 (a stale/affected/superseded flag on a requirement, a commissioning evidence id, a punch item, a vendor document, a review decision, a concession, a functional test and a dossier id reopens exactly the stated link, earliest link first); acceptance 7 (the punch rule interplay of 5.2: one of 140/141/142 while open, only 144 when closed without a closure record, 151 plus 180 when flagged); acceptance 8 (assembly order of 4.7 and review_decisions surviving it); the 4.10 worked numbers 7 d, 12 d and mean 9.5 d; every link L1..L8 as the first broken link. Boundaries: 60- and 61-character system id bodies, a name that slugs to nothing, derived id collision, closure on the acceptance day against the day after, closed_at before raised_at, a datetime with an offset crossing the UTC day boundary, an impossible calendar date, concession status raised / approved / accepted / closed and kind concession / deviation, docFinal by status alone, functional-test result ' Passed ' against 'conditional pass', a condition affecting a gate above the target, and requirements_na with and without a reason. 3 cases are marked disputable and 4 carry a recorded spec ambiguity. Added by adjudication: the two exception sources of 4.9 that nothing graded (an accepted_exception item and an open carry-over item inside a closed link), and 25 checks that pin link_status, link_own_ok, links_closed and the next gate after a failing R62 - the headline claim "a link is closed only when every upstream link is closed" rested on 5 graded comparisons and now rests on 27. Second adjudication pass 2026-09-23: 7 further checks pin the three spec-changelog resolutions that no case graded - punch[id] read as the first row of a duplicated id, the system field of the project-level orphan findings COM-R-048 and COM-R-170, and COM-R-100 de-duplicated to one finding when two evaluated systems share a name.
